label: TV Series
rubric: Critical acclaim · Cultural impact & longevity · Fan devotion/rewatchability · Awards/prestige

entries.name: Breaking Bad
entries.rationale: Near-perfect character arc and one of the highest-rated series ever recorded.

entries.name: The Sopranos
entries.rationale: Widely credited with starting the prestige television era outright.

entries.name: The Wire
entries.rationale: Novelistic scope and social depth that critics still treat as the ceiling.

entries.name: Better Call Saul
entries.rationale: A prequel that many argue matches or exceeds its acclaimed predecessor.

entries.name: Succession
entries.rationale: Awards-sweeping dialogue-driven drama that dominated cultural conversation.

entries.name: Mad Men
entries.rationale: Meticulous period drama with four consecutive Outstanding Drama wins.

entries.name: Seinfeld
entries.rationale: Reinvented the sitcom and left permanent marks on everyday language.

entries.name: Chernobyl
entries.rationale: A near-flawless limited series with overwhelming critical consensus.

entries.name: The Simpsons
entries.rationale: Its golden-age run is arguably the most influential comedy writing ever televised.

entries.name: Fleabag
entries.rationale: Two short seasons that swept the Emmys and redefined the fourth wall.

entries.name: The Twilight Zone
entries.rationale: The anthology blueprint that every genre series since has borrowed from.

entries.name: Twin Peaks
entries.rationale: Broke every network convention and made prestige weirdness viable.

entries.name: The Bear
entries.rationale: Awards-dominating and intensely acclaimed with remarkable tonal control.

entries.name: Severance
entries.rationale: Original high-concept premise executed with unusual precision and design.

entries.name: Avatar: The Last Airbender
entries.rationale: Animated series with all-ages acclaim and one of TV's best-plotted arcs.

entries.name: Game of Thrones
entries.rationale: The biggest global TV event of its decade, held back by its final season.

entries.name: The Office (US)
entries.rationale: Extraordinary rewatch numbers and a permanent streaming comfort-watch staple.

entries.name: Curb Your Enthusiasm
entries.rationale: Improvised comedy that stayed sharp across an unusually long run.

entries.name: The Crown
entries.rationale: Lavish, awards-heavy historical drama with sustained global viewership.

entries.name: The Last of Us
entries.rationale: The rare video game adaptation that critics and fans both embraced.

entries.name: Arrested Development
entries.rationale: Densely constructed comedy writing that rewards repeat viewing heavily.

entries.name: Friends
entries.rationale: Enormous enduring popularity and syndication value, modest critical standing.

entries.name: Black Mirror
entries.rationale: Anthology with real cultural bite, though episode quality varies widely.

entries.name: True Detective
entries.rationale: A first season regarded as an all-timer; later seasons uneven.

entries.name: Stranger Things
entries.rationale: Massive streaming phenomenon with strong nostalgia pull, lighter prestige.

entries.name: Rick and Morty
entries.rationale: Inventive animated sci-fi with a huge, vocal fanbase.

entries.name: Sherlock
entries.rationale: Hugely popular reinvention, though its later seasons divided viewers.

entries.name: Squid Game
entries.rationale: The biggest non-English streaming hit ever, more phenomenon than prestige.

entries.name: Ted Lasso
entries.rationale: Awards-winning feel-good comedy with broad appeal but a mixed later run.

entries.name: Lost
entries.rationale: Defined appointment-viewing mystery TV; the ending remains contested.
